bullets.title: Q2 2026: NDX +27%, SOX +88% — best quarterly returns on record
bullets.body: The Nasdaq 100 posted its best quarter since Q2 2020 (+27%), while the SOX delivered its strongest quarterly return since inception in 1993/1994 (+87–88%), driven by AI capex enthusiasm and memory supply tightness. MU and SNDK led with +241.7% and +257.9% respectively in Q2; tech sector overall gained +31.6% vs. S&P 500 +14.87%.

bullets.title: June was a rougher month — Mag 7 shed $2T, Nasdaq -2.81%
bullets.body: Despite the stellar quarter, June 2026 saw the S&P 500 -1.06% and Nasdaq -2.81%, with the Mag 7 losing over $2T in value — worst performance in over a year. MSFT -17.2%, AMZN -11.9%, META -10.9% were the worst performers, as AI ROI concerns mounted alongside open-source competition and companies pushing back on AI spend. Semiconductors bucked the trend with SOX +11.1% and memory +16.7% in June.

bullets.title: Today's tape: narrow leadership — NDX +1.7% but 60% of SPX names declined
bullets.body: Tech led the session with hyperscaler dip-buying (AMZN, GOOGL) on AI toll-booth and valuation narratives, but nearly 60% of SPX stocks closed lower despite index gains. Equal-weight S&P lagged cap-weighted, and the momentum trade stalled into the close. Semis, airlines, and memory led; hotels, cruise lines, REITs, and banks lagged.

bullets.title: Fed pivoting hawkish: dot plot implies hikes, Cleveland Fed warns AI fueling inflation
bullets.body: Fed funds futures now price ~33bp of hikes through year-end 2026, with the dot plot showing 12.5bp of hikes expected. Fed Chair Warsh scrapped forward guidance in his first meeting, and Cleveland Fed's Hammack explicitly warned that AI demand is stoking inflation and rate hikes may be necessary — framing AI as an inflationary force, not just an energy story. Treasury yields rose 5–8bp across the curve today.

bullets.title: JOLTS upside surprise: 7,594K vs 6,975K consensus; labor market 'solid, not strong'
bullets.body: May JOLTS job openings came in well above expectations at 7,594K vs. 6,975K consensus, though the underlying picture remains a low-hire, low-fire economy (layoff rate 1.1%, hire rate 3.3%). Net hiring has increased since fall 2025, layoffs are at 4-year lows, and QCEW data suggest positive benchmark revisions to NFP are likely. Conference Board labor differential, however, deteriorated to its worst since 2021 — historically a signal of rising unemployment.

bullets.title: NFP Thursday is the next key macro event; JPM Feroli expects 125K vs Street 110K
bullets.body: JPM economist Feroli forecasts June NFP at 125K (vs. Street consensus 110K, prior 172K), 4.3% unemployment, and +0.2% MoM earnings. Options pricing implies a 1.2% SPX move for the July 2 expiry; JPM scenario analysis skews bullish with 40% probability of a 100K–130K outcome. ISM Manufacturing for June is expected at 55.0 (consensus 53.8), which would be the highest reading since June 2022.

bullets.title: Iran geopolitical risk reignited: no direct US-Iran talks, Hormuz passage limited to 60 days
bullets.body: Iran's foreign minister stated no direct US-Iran meetings are scheduled in Doha; indirect talks will proceed with Qatar as mediator. Iran's parliamentary speaker noted toll-free Strait of Hormuz passage would be limited to 60 days. These headlines drove 4–5bp of today's Treasury yield move and contributed to ISM strength partly reflecting supply chain front-loading from Middle East conflict risk.

bullets.title: June consumer confidence missed badly: 91.2 vs 94.7 consensus; jobs hardest to find in 5+ years
bullets.body: June consumer confidence printed 91.2 vs. 94.7 consensus, with May revised lower to 90.6 from 93.1. The labor market differential fell to its weakest since 2021, with jobs now the hardest to find in over five years. This offsets the upbeat JOLTS headline and raises questions about consumer durability heading into Q3.

bullets.title: July catalyst calendar: tariff expiration 7/24, FOMC 7/29, TSMC earnings 7/16, AMD AI conference 7/22
bullets.body: GS TMT desk flags July as historically bullish for NDX (higher in 17 of 18 years, averaging +4.35%). Key binary events include the 10% tariff expiration on 7/24 and FOMC on 7/29. Semis catalysts include TSMC Japan Symposium (7/3), TSLA GigaTexas update (7/7), TSM earnings (7/16), and AMD Advancing AI conference (7/22–23). CRWD stock split effective 7/2.

bullets.title: JPM global thematic: Physical AI is the new US-China battleground; consumer recovery in H2
bullets.body: JPM's June thematic views flag Physical AI (robotics/humanoids) as the primary US-China competition arena, with US considering action against Chinese robotics given ~80% humanoid market share. China's 15th Five-Year Plan targets RMB 2–5 trillion AI data center buildout by 2030; South Korea announced a $3.1T semiconductor/AI/robotics investment plan. Separately, JPM sees global consumer macro shifting from stagflation to recovery/expansion in H2 2026, with Chase card data showing Q2 spending at +5.1% and upper-income cohorts at +6–7%.

bullets.title: AI inference costs dropping 50%; AWS $1B new AI unit; Google hitting record power/water use
bullets.body: OpenAI discovered an inference optimization cutting model running costs by ~50%. AWS announced a $1B investment in a new AI unit for customers building AI systems. Google's AI buildout drove record electricity and water consumption. Cleveland Fed's Hammack specifically framed AI as an inflationary demand driver — a new policy risk angle for the sector.

bullets.title: Credit markets benign: clients lifting tail hedges amid low vol; HYG/LQD flows constructive
bullets.body: MS credit desk reports funding conditions easing broadly (HYG 1m swap reset -45, LQD revcons near -30). Clients are lifting outright tail hedges in IG and HY given low implied vols, while fast money supplies vol in September strangles/straddles. iBoxx and credit ETF flows skewed to buyers; 40-/20-delta payer spreads favored as more efficient hedges than equity vol.

bullets.title: BofA holds S&P 7100 target — implies ~5% downside from here
bullets.body: BofA left its 2026 S&P 500 target unchanged at 7,100, implying roughly 5% downside from current levels. The firm cites reversal of multiple-boosting levers including asset-lightness, balance sheet strength, capital discipline, and earnings quality. This is a notable cautious signal against a backdrop of strong Q2 performance and bullish July seasonality.

bullets.title: Retail investor Mag 7 activity at 4-year lows despite record quarter
bullets.body: Despite the NDX posting its best quarter since 2020, retail investor activity in Mag 7 stocks is at its lowest level in four years. This suggests the Q2 rally was institutional/systematic rather than retail-driven, which could have implications for the sustainability and character of any continuation.

bullets.title: FTC reportedly moving to ban Chinese inverter imports; ENPH and solar names rally
bullets.body: The Trump administration via FTC is reportedly looking to ban inverter imports to the US, citing concerns about China's ability to disrupt US power supplies. Solar and fuel cell names rallied on the news (ENPH +1.9%, SEDG +5.6%), while BE surged ~10% on a separate $25B AI infrastructure partnership expansion with Brookfield — a 5-fold increase to build rapid power for AI data centers.

bullets.title: Open USD stablecoin launches with 100+ partners; negative for Circle, mixed for Coinbase
bullets.body: Open Standard launched the Open USD stablecoin with 100+ partners including Visa, Mastercard, Stripe, Coinbase, Robinhood, Shopify, and Affirm, featuring no mint/burn fees and majority reserve income sharing. KeyBanc views this as negative for Circle (USDC market share erosion) and mostly positive for Coinbase as a partner. This is a structural shift in stablecoin competitive dynamics.

bullets.title: AI inference architecture debate: GPUs 'inadequate' for post-ChatGPT workloads, TSMC relationships key
bullets.body: Etched founders argue inference — not training — will be one of the largest tech markets next decade, requiring purpose-built chips optimized for throughput, latency, and power efficiency rather than current GPU architectures. Hyperscalers building internal AI chips seek 'good enough' NVIDIA alternatives to reduce dependence, not category-leading hardware. TSMC's engineering collaboration and customer support relationships are cited as the key differentiator.

bullets.title: Q2 earnings expectations remain strong at 22% growth; semis driving ~47% of S&P EPS growth
bullets.body: Q2 S&P 500 earnings growth is expected at ~22.0% YoY (down from 28.8% in Q1), with semiconductors alone expected to drive approximately 47% of the index's 23% YoY earnings growth in Q2. AI capex and oil price tailwinds are cited as key drivers alongside the continued memory upcycle.

bullets.title: US retail web traffic surged +32% YoY in June week 4 — strongest in 12+ weeks
bullets.body: Citi's web traffic tracker showed US retail web traffic averaging +32% YoY in June Week 4, the first time exceeding 30% in over 12 weeks, aided by temperatures running 3.6°F cooler vs. prior year. WSM brands (Pottery Barn, West Elm) showed consistently strong traffic the past two months; CRI accelerated to +56%, NKE to +13%, while TGT decelerated and ASO fell.

bullets.title: Software RSU grants rebounding in 1Q26 but share count dilution surging on lower stock prices
bullets.body: Enterprise software sector RSU grant values fell 28.3% in CY25 vs. CY24 under investor dilution pressure, but 1Q26 median grants bounced +12.5% YoY. The catch: total shares granted jumped 52.2% YoY, primarily because lower stock prices required more shares to deliver the same dollar value of compensation — a dilution risk that persists for names still trading at depressed levels.
